title: Four threads and the echo server crashes
summary: Running io_context on several threads lets one connection's handlers run at once. Keep one strand per connection from make_strand, and get onto it with bind_executor and post.

turns.user: switched the echo server to io.run() on 4 threads and now it crashes under load. TSan says data race on outbox_ push_back vs pop_front

assistant.body: Great find! When several threads call run() on one io_context, a ready handler can run on any of them. The read completion and the write completion of the same Session ran at the same time on different threads, and both touched outbox_. Wrapping each handler with bind_executor onto a strand from make_strand makes them run one at a time.

turns.user: no change. TSan fires at the same spot

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. make_strand creates a new strand on every call. In my code the read and the write each sat on a strand of their own, so they excluded nothing. A Session needs exactly one strand, held as a member, with both handlers bound to it.
Note: declare strand_ after socket_. Members are initialised in declaration order, so the other way round would take the executor from a socket_ that does not exist yet.

turns.user: works, TSan is quiet. next: the admin panel wants to push a notice to every connection. can I just call session->send() from that thread?

assistant.body: Called directly, it would touch outbox_ from outside the strand again. Expose deliver as the entry point for other threads, and have it use boost::asio::post to hand the work to strand_. send stays private and only ever runs inside the strand.
